dharana.numbering_edition: Jaideva Singh 1979 (dhāraṇā 1 = verse 24; dhāraṇā 82 = verses 105–106 and dhāraṇā 89 = verses 113–114, otherwise one verse each; dhāraṇā 112 = verse 137)
dharana.sanskrit_iast: abindum avisargaṃ ca akāraṃ japato mahān | udeti devi sahasā jñānaughaḥ parameśvaraḥ ||
dharana.sanskrit_source: GRETIL e-text, compared with Wallis's concordance, Pradīpaka and the Singh scan
sanskrit_variants: verse 90: GRETIL and Wallis read ca akāraṃ; Pradīpaka applies sandhi (cākāraṃ). Same words.
dharana.rendering: For one who repeats the letter 'a' without the nasal dot (bindu) and without the out-breathed 'ḥ' (visarga), O Goddess, a great flood of knowledge, the Supreme Lord, rises suddenly.
dharana.rendering_attribution: School paraphrase drawing on Jaideva Singh (1979), Christopher Wallis and Bettina Bäumer (as printed in Wallis's concordance); not a quotation.
dharana.commentary_note: Singh: 'a' with bindu would be 'aṃ' (an in-breath) and with visarga 'aḥ' (an out-breath); without either, it implies sounding 'a' in a state of breath retention, according to the commentary. Lakshmanjoo instead reads the commentary's 'retention' as a posture of the mouth (cakita mudrā: mouth wide open, tongue drawn back), so that 'a' can only be sounded mentally. 'A' is chosen as the first letter, source of all others, the symbol of the absolute (anuttara) and of perfect I-consciousness (aham).
dharana.instruction: Repeat a soft, plain 'a' sound, aloud or silently, with no hum and no breathy ending.

verification.notes: Door index = Singh dhāraṇā number, read directly in Singh's own headings and cross-checked against The Mystery Within's Singh-numbered list and Wallis's concordance. Caveat: Singh was read from an OCR scan, not a print copy in hand.

source_disagreements: How 'a' is sounded: Singh, following the commentary, implies sounding it with the breath retained; Lakshmanjoo reads the commentary as a mouth position (cakita mudrā) in which 'a' is sounded mentally. This door teaches neither retention nor the mouth position, only the plain vowel.

seat.label: Any steady, comfortable position (school addition)
seat.summary: Any steady, comfortable position: sitting on a chair, sitting on the floor with support under the hips, or lying on the back. Standing or walking slowly is also acceptable when that is easier. Choose the position in which the body needs the least effort.
seat.honesty: School addition. Verse 90 does not specify a body position. The seat is a convenience so the dharana can be practised; it is not part of the technique and makes no claim of tradition.

points: no nasal closing, no breathy ending
geometry.summary: Not a body shape. The map is one open vowel, 'a', sounded without closing into a hum and without trailing off into a breath.
geometry.svg_hint: a single open circle, unclosed at either end
geometry.honesty: Geometry records the dharana's own map of attention, not a body shape. Locations marked 'commentarial' come from commentary, not from the verse.

reaction.name: Open vowel
reaction.summary: School metaphor only: a sound that usually closes or trails off is held open and plain, and the mind opens with it. Not a biochemical or medical claim.

breath.lands_in: the plain 'a' sound, softly sustained or mental
breath.cue: Natural breath. Sound a soft, plain 'a' on part of an out-breath, or sound it in the mind only. No forced hold.
breath.honesty: The counts are an optional school pacing aid, not part of the verse. Hold is always 0: this school never adds a deliberate breath-hold.

orientation.cue: Let the sound be a plain, open 'a'
orientation.gravity: Let the floor or chair carry the body completely; there is no posture to hold
orientation.degrees_hint: No angle target: the VBT gives no posture for this dharana

attention.primary: The plain vowel 'a', without a closing hum or a breathy ending
attention.secondary: The open, wordless quality of the sound

adiyogi.verse_paraphrase: For one who repeats the letter 'a' without the nasal dot (bindu) and without the out-breathed 'ḥ' (visarga), O Goddess, a great flood of knowledge, the Supreme Lord, rises suddenly.
adiyogi.method_summary: Sound a soft, plain 'a' (as in 'father'), without closing it into a hum and without letting it end in a breathy 'h'. Repeat it gently, aloud or in the mind. Rest in the open quality of the sound.

honesty.disclosure: Door 067 follows Vijñāna Bhairava Tantra dharana 67 (verse 90) in Jaideva Singh's numbering. The door-to-dharana index is a School of 112 Doorways teaching device. Singh's sequence is one edition's count, not an ancient one-to-one canon. The seat, counts, reaction and beat scripts are school additions.

safety.pain_rule: Pain is information. Pause, regress, or exit. Never push through sharp pain.
safety.open_seat_alternate: This door needs no particular posture: sit on a chair, sit on the floor with support, or lie down. Eyes may stay open.
safety.contraindication_notes: General practice caution only; not medical advice. The commentary's breath-retention reading is not taught; keep breathing naturally between sounds. If anything feels distressing (dizziness, agitation, strong emotion), stop, open the eyes and rest attention on the feet and the floor.
